scheme_name: Pre-Matric Scholarship for the Students of Notified Tribes and Denotified Tribes Castes
description:
The Pre-Matric Scholarship for the Students of Notified Tribes and Denotified Tribes Castes is a significant initiative by the Government of India aimed at promoting education among students belonging to specific marginalized communities. 

This scheme was launched on 1st July 2012 under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs. 

The primary objective of this scholarship is to provide financial assistance to students from notified tribes and denotified tribes. 

The scheme aims to reduce dropout rates among students belonging to these communities and encourage them to pursue their education. 

The scholarship covers students studying in classes 1 to 10. 

The specific goal is to ensure that students from these communities complete their education at least up to the secondary level. 

The government has set a measurable target to increase the enrollment of students from these communities in schools by 20% annually. 

The benefits under this scholarship scheme include a monthly scholarship amount that varies based on the class of the student. 

For students in classes 1 to 5, the scholarship amount is ₹1,000 per annum. 

For students in classes 6 to 8, the scholarship amount is ₹3,000 per annum. 

For students in classes 9 and 10, the scholarship amount is ₹4,000 per annum. 

In addition to the scholarship amount, students are also provided with a maintenance allowance. 

The maintenance allowance is ₹500 per month for students in classes 6 to 8. 

For students in classes 9 and 10, the maintenance allowance is ₹1,000 per month. 

The total financial assistance can therefore reach up to ₹10,000 per annum for students in classes 9 and 10. 

Eligibility criteria for this scholarship are clearly defined. 

Students must belong to notified tribes or denotified tribes as per the government’s classification. 

The family income of the applicant should not exceed ₹2.5 lakh per annum. 

Students must be enrolled in recognized schools, either government or private. 

There are no specific educational qualifications required for the students themselves, as the scheme is aimed at those currently enrolled in school. 

The application process for the Pre-Matric Scholarship is straightforward. 

Students must obtain the scholarship application form from the respective state government’s education department or the Ministry of Tribal Affairs’ website. 

The application form must be filled out completely and accurately. 

Required documents include a caste certificate issued by a competent authority. 

Students must also provide proof of income, such as an income certificate from the local revenue office. 

A copy of the student’s bank passbook is also required to facilitate the disbursement of funds. 

Additionally, students must submit their school admission certificate and a recent passport-sized photograph. 

Once the application is completed, it should be submitted to the school authorities. 

The school will then forward the applications to the respective district welfare officer. 

The timeline for application submission typically begins at the start of the academic year. 

Students are advised to submit their applications before the deadline set by the state government. 

Disbursement of the scholarship amount occurs after the applications are verified and approved by the district welfare officer. 

Payments are generally made directly to the students' bank accounts. 

The frequency of disbursement is usually once a year. 

However, some states may have different schedules for disbursement based on their administrative processes. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Tribal Affairs at the central level. 

At the state level, the scheme is executed through the respective State Tribal Welfare Departments. 

Contact details for the Ministry of Tribal Affairs can be found on their official website. 

The Ministry can be reached at their headquarters located in New Delhi. 

The scheme has seen a significant uptake since its launch. 

In the financial year 2020-2021, approximately 1.5 million students benefited from the scholarship. 

The total allocation for the scheme in the Union Budget for the financial year 2021-2022 was ₹1,200 crores. 

This indicates the government’s commitment to enhancing educational opportunities for marginalized communities. 

The scholarship has played a crucial role in improving literacy rates among notified tribes and denotified tribes. 

According to the 2011 Census, the literacy rate among Scheduled Tribes was 59%. 

This scheme aims to bridge the gap and increase this percentage significantly. 

The government is also working on awareness programs to ensure that eligible students are informed about the scholarship. 

Workshops and seminars are conducted in tribal areas to educate families about the benefits of the scheme. 

The Pre-Matric Scholarship is part of a broader set of initiatives aimed at empowering tribal communities. 

The government has also introduced post-matric scholarships and skill development programs for these communities. 

These initiatives collectively aim to uplift the socio-economic status of tribal populations in India. 

The scheme is monitored regularly to assess its impact and effectiveness. 

Feedback from beneficiaries is collected to make necessary adjustments to the scheme. 

The government is committed to ensuring that no eligible student is left behind. 

In conclusion, the Pre-Matric Scholarship for the Students of Notified Tribes and Denotified Tribes Castes is a vital program that aims to enhance educational access and retention among marginalized communities. 

With specific financial benefits and a structured application process, it serves as a crucial support system for students in India. 

The scheme reflects the government’s dedication to promoting education as a means of empowerment for tribal populations.
